title: RAG source-identity testcases and prompt corpus
body:
Purpose:
This working doc collects a focused prompt corpus and testcase matrix for evaluating model behavior around source identity in RAG flows: i.e., does the generator correctly (1) attribute quoted snippets to the exact source document, (2) avoid inventing attributions when provenance is absent, and (3) refuse or hedge when sources contradict or are insufficient.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target models: onboarding candidates (open and finetuned) before they are admitted to the hosted catalog.
- Retrieval backend: dense + BM25 hybrid. Test harness can fake retrievals by returning curated passages with explicit metadata (doc id, title, url).
- We evaluate generation-level outputs (text) and metadata-level outputs (returned citations list). For now this corpus prioritizes human-readable text checklists and automated string-match pass/fail hints.
- Not exhaustive; this is intended to catch common failure classes found in production RAG integrations.

High-level test categories (with informal priority):
1) Exact-quote attribution (HIGH) — generator must place exact quote and attach correct source label or citation marker.
2) Paraphrase attribution (MED) — paraphrases should still reference the correct source when derived from a single doc.
3) False attribution (CRITICAL) — generator must not attribute content to a document that does not contain it.
4) Missing provenance refusal (HIGH) — when claims cannot be traced to any retrieved doc, prefer refusal/hedge or explicit "no source found" statement.
5) Conflicting sources (MED) — when retrievals contain contradictory claims, model should surface ambiguity and cite both or refuse to choose.
6) Partial grounding (LOW) — when snippet supports only part of an asserted fact, model should avoid overclaiming.

Scoring rubric (for quick automated / human review):
- PASS: Output includes correct citation identifiers matching provided retrieval set and claims are faithful.
- PASS-WARN: Citation present but paraphrase subtly adds unverified detail (flag for human review).
- FAIL: Attribution incorrect (points to doc that doesn't contain claim), or model fabricates a source (e.g., invents a URL or author), or fails to refuse when retrieval is empty.

Quick notes on implementation in harness:
- Each testcase will provide: prompt, retrieval bundle (list of passages + metadata), expected citation tokens (doc ids or titles), and assertion type (must-attach | may-attach | must-refuse).
- For human review, include examples of tolerable paraphrase (keywords vs new facts).
- Use both inline citation style (e.g., "(Doc: A)") and superscript numeric markers to exercise different output behaviors.

Seed prompt corpus (domain-angled examples) — keep these short and adaptable for parameter sweeps:

Testcase RAG-SI-001: direct-quote-attach
- Prompt: "According to the provided documents, quote the sentence that describes the company's data retention policy and cite the source."
- Retrieval bundle: one passage from doc-id: HR-2023-policy with the line: "All customer data is retained for a maximum of 90 days unless otherwise contracted." metadata: title=HR Data Retention (2023), url=https://intranet/docs/hr-data-2023
- Expectation: Model outputs the exact sentence in quotes and includes the HR Data Retention (2023) citation.
- Assertion: must-attach

Testcase RAG-SI-002: paraphrase-still-attribute
- Prompt: "Summarize the incident response timeline from the retrieved documents and say which doc the summary is based on."
- Retrieval bundle: single doc: IR-brief-2024 contains a 3-step timeline.
- Expectation: Paraphrase is acceptable but model must state "Based on IR-brief-2024" or similar.
- Assertion: must-attach (paraphrase tolerated)

Testcase RAG-SI-003: false-attribution-detect
- Prompt: "List the export compliance rules and cite the source document."
- Retrieval bundle: doc A (exports-summary) covers export thresholds but does not mention specific sanctions lists; doc B (sanctions-notice) is absent.
- Model failure mode to catch: model asserts specific sanctioned countries and cites exports-summary even though that doc lacks those details.
- Expectation: If specific sanctions are not in bundle, the model should either refuse or say "no retrieved doc mentions sanctions lists".
- Assertion: must-refuse or must-not-attach

Testcase RAG-SI-004: invented-url-refusal
- Prompt: "Cite the source for the claim that the product was deprecated in Q1 2024."
- Retrieval bundle: empty (simulating no hits)
- Expectation: Model should not invent a URL or doc id (common bad behavior). Acceptable outputs: "I couldn't find a source in the retrieved documents" or refusal.
- Assertion: must-refuse

Testcase RAG-SI-005: conflicting-sources-both-cited
- Prompt: "Several documents mention disk encryption status. Reconcile the discrepancy and cite sources."
- Retrieval bundle: doc-X says "encryption at rest enabled"; doc-Y says "encryption rollout scheduled".
- Expectation: Model notes the contradiction and cites both doc-X and doc-Y, avoids asserting a single ground truth.
- Assertion: must-attach-multiple

Testcase RAG-SI-006: partial-support-avoid-overclaim
- Prompt: "Does the product support continuous backups every hour? Provide supporting citations."
- Retrieval bundle: passage indicates backups run nightly.
- Expectation: Model must not claim hourly backups. Correct answer: "No evidence of hourly backups in retrieved docs; the docs state nightly backups (doc Z)."
- Assertion: must-not-attach (to hourly claim) / must-attach (to nightly claim)

Edge-case probes (short/fast checks):
- Embedded-quotation-swap: Passages contain two similar sentences with different subjects; check that the model doesn't swap the subject when quoting.
- Author-mismatch: Retriever returns passage with author metadata; check model uses the attached author, not a guessed one.
- Locale-sensitive cites: Dates formatted differently in retrieval bundle; model should quote the date string as-is when attributing.

Failure classification and tickets:
- Fabricated-source (high priority): model outputs made-up URL or doc id. Create jira:RAG-712 if seen.
- Attribution-swap (medium): assigns content to wrong doc. Create jira:RAG-713.
- Overclaim (medium): infers extra facts that aren't in text. Create jira:RAG-714.
- Silent-hallucination (critical): model asserts fact with no citation. Create jira:RAG-715.

Regression report template (for each model run):
- model_name: string
- run_date: date
- total_tests: int (put as free-text in harness export)
- pass_rate: percentage string
- failing_tests: comma-separated ids
- top_failure_modes: comma-separated labels
- sample-failure-output: short excerpt (for reviewers)

Notes to reviewers / TODOs:
- Add variant where retrievals include near-duplicate passages from multiple docs to test de-dup logic.
- Instrument automated matching to allow fuzzy match for paraphrases but strict match for direct quotes.
- Collect 50+ negative examples (claims not present) to stress false-attribution threshold.
- Cross-link to product's rollout guidelines: confluence:APPLIEDML-998 (see linked_artifacts).

Conversation snippets / quick manual checks (copy-paste friendly):
- "Quote the sentence about retention."
- "Which document says backups are nightly?"
- "I can't find sanctions info — did any doc mention it?"

Final thought (working):
This corpus is intentionally pragmatic — focused on behaviors we see break in production RAG: invented sources, silent hallucinations, and brittle paraphrase attribution. Keep prompts short, retrieval bundles minimal and explicit, and prefer failure-driven examples. After a round of model runs we can expand into templated permutations (change doc titles, add noise, swap authors) and tune pass/fail thresholds.

-- Maya R. (notes)
